j1.calculation: (7.0x0.12)+(7.0x0.16)+(6.8x0.12)+(6.8x0.08)+(7.4x0.08)+(7.0x0.06)+(7.5x0.10)+(7.5x0.08)+(8.4x0.10)+(8.0x0.06)+(7.4x0.04) = 0.84+1.12+0.816+0.544+0.592+0.42+0.75+0.60+0.84+0.48+0.296 = 7.298, which rounds to 7.30. No axis moved more than 1.0 from my cut-2 card. Biggest moves are +0.1 each on Color, VO sync, Accuracy and Writing, and all of them are the film changing, not my standard.
concrete_defects: 127.6s (f127.6, filmstrips 43/45), S16 closing hero: the TENANT FIRST boxcar sits on bare snow with no rails under it, while the right-hand leg of rails runs empty off the bottom right. The fork's whole argument is which leg gets laid first, and the empty-boxcar leg doesn't exist under the boxcar. This frame is also where the post's question lands.

123.75-128s (filmstrips 43 and 45): across both strips the second switch lever barely moves. The beat is written as 'begins a slow lean toward RULES FIRST' and then 'holding mid-throw', but almost all of the 7% measured change is the lamp and plates. The film ends on a held prop with no anticipation, travel or settle.

26.5s (filmstrip 12): the 'plain grey diesel pulling boxcars' stays put across all 8 frames. Only the smoke puff and the PENDING AGENDA plate change. A train sold as passing the switch doesn't translate, so the lever-rattle 'as the cars pass' beat at 28.8s has nothing driving it.

127.6s: the RECONSIDERATION DUE / NOVEMBER 30TH plate sits on top of the small main stand's lamp, the very lamp the beat says is 'flaring' behind. BOARD · FRIDAY carries a lighter halo rectangle that doesn't match the other plates' shadow treatment.

76.6s (f076.6), S10: the DECEMBER 7TH plate and its vertical line sit at x~762, but the ruler's DEC 7TH tick is at x~793, half a tie off. The DNR 'NOVEMBER 30TH' label sits at x~420 against its ruler tick at x~355. The NOV 25TH ruler label from the strip at 72s no longer shows. On a 'count the ties' beat, a misregistered count undercuts the device. The top ~430px is also empty cream, the most dead space in the film.

25.5s (f025.5), S5: a 'NOV 27TH' table card pokes out under the SET TO RESUME FRIDAY plate, clipped by it, so the same date shows twice with one copy partly hidden. The plate stack also covers the chair backs. It reads as a layering accident, not a staged prop.

105-109s (f107.2, f108.8): the dial's 'MOSTLY OPPOSED' legend runs into the dial rim, and the final D is struck through by the bezel stroke. It's still legible, so no blocker, but it's a text-fit flaw on the payoff gauge.

86.8s (f086.8): the MORATORIUM UNTIL RULES card covers the top of the Kreiss-Tomkins Suit's head, and the same string is also plated above, so the line appears twice on one frame. The KREISS-TOMKINS name card floats in front of his leg.

45.9-48s (f045.9, f048.0): the Plural quote is on screen twice, as a top plate and on the billboard, and the THE PITCH stamp is cut off by the billboard's top edge. A third stack of the same words in the frame is crowding, not emphasis.

Throughout (f005.1, f046-048, f086.8, f094.5, f107.2, f117.4): the same foreground dressing kit (snow-capped tie stack, loose rail, steaming bucket, signal post) repeats in about 10 shots. Characters are still plain flat fills with tan heads and read plainer than the form-shaded switch stands and boxcars.
Typography, whole film: every plate and caption is in one mono face, and I found no Fraunces anywhere, so the type system has no second voice. Kinetic type is limited to plates sliding in.
Credits (f130.1+): the source list omits the Mat-Su Sentinel, which the 101.1s plate cites on screen ('DNR, PER MAT-SU SENTINEL').

j1.editor_notes_for_email: This is a single standing-seat card at 7.30, which clears the 7.0 bar with no hard blocker, so per panel_protocol.md the other two seats should be convened. If the panel wants one high-leverage fix, it's the 125-129s ending: put the boxcar on rails on the TENANT FIRST leg and give the second switch lever a real eased throw with overshoot and settle. Before posting: add the Mat-Su Sentinel to the credits source list, since it is cited on screen at 101s. The post's last paragraph ('court AI infrastructure money from firmer ground') is an editorial stance; it's sourced-adjacent but reads as advocacy.

concrete_defects: 72.0-76.6s (filmstrips 12_ties_..._26 and 5_bare_ties_..._27, measured change 1.8% and 2.5%; still f076.6): the VO says 'Count the ties', but the DNR branch never shows 30 countable ties. The track runs off the right edge, only about 12 ties are visible, and the bare ties at left are faint dashes. It is the thesis beat of the film and the image doesn't pay it off. It is also the most static stretch in the film.

76.6s (f076.6): the ILLUSTRATION tag sits on top of the timeline ruler's first tick and hides the NOV 25TH start label, so the 12-day count has no visible origin. The frame is also a flat diagram with about 22% empty space above and below, which breaks from the shaded world in every other shot.

61.6-63.0s (f063.0, filmstrip the_switch_points_beside_the_parcel_23): the caption box covers the switch points and the stand's base, and that is exactly the board-flagged hero action ('switch points slide over toward a siding', with a boom SFX). The hit plays under the caption.

105.2-108.8s (f107.2, f108.8): the dial label 'MOSTLY OPPOSED' is jammed against the gauge rim. The M touches the left rim and the final D collides with a tick mark, so at phone size it reads 'OPPOSEĐ'. Preflight didn't flag it, but it is the on-screen number/label risk the rubric names.

79.5-81.5s (filmstrip the_faceless_kreiss_tomkins_suit_the_29) and 9.2-10.5s (filmstrip a_faceless_suit_with_a_boxed_name_ca_5): as the Suit walks in, his name card is cropped at the frame edge ('KINS', 'OMKINS', 'S-TOMKINS') and his body covers the date board ('DE  7TH', 'V 25TH'). Plates get occluded mid-read in two shots.
25.5s (f025.5): the 'SET TO RESUME FRIDAY' plate overlaps the in-world 'NOV 27TH' table card and cuts off the top of its letters. Plate on in-world type.

117.4s and 127.6s (f117.4, f127.6): the RULES ties are drawn as horizontal labelled planks pasted over the rails. On the receding track at 127.6 they ignore its perspective, so they read as stickers, not laid ties. Also at 127.6 the RECONSIDERATION DUE plate covers the far stand's lamp, and the TENANT FIRST plate floats over the trees with no post.

127.8-128.9s (filmstrip the_second_switch_s_lever_holding_mi_45): the final 'mid-throw' lever is effectively frozen. Only the lamp changes, so the closing question lands on a held frame with no settle or anticipation.

Film-wide (stills f005.1, f019.0, f094.5, f117.4): the top 22-25% of nearly every 9:16 frame is empty cream sky, and two or three stacked plates sit on the mountain line. The hero props sit low, the frame reads top-heavy and empty, and the plate stacks crowd the horizon.

Film-wide (f019.0, f094.5): the faceless Suits use near-flat suit fills, oval hands and no rim light, while the boxcars, switch stands and binders carry gradients and contact shadows. The characters lag the props on finish.
0.0-2.6s (filmstrip the_faceless_cast_iron_switch_stand_1, 5.9% change): the open is a near-static landscape with a plate. The line is good but nothing in frame stops the scroll.
Typography: every plate, caption and credit is in the mono face. I see no Fraunces display moment anywhere, so the type system reads as one register and stays static.

Music: the bed is a stock Kevin MacLeod 'Easy Lemon', a light and generic cue for a governance-handoff story. It is credited and ducked correctly, but it doesn't follow the arc. The SFX are dense and the ambience is audible in the gaps, which saves the axis at 7.

post.txt: 'Rules first would stall no project anyone has named there' is broader than the sourced claim (AIDEA's July op-ed and its November spokesperson). The VO's 'no project AIDEA has named' is the defensible version. The closing line 'court AI infrastructure money from firmer ground' is editorial advocacy beyond the even-handed film.

0.0-5.1s (filmstrips 1 and 2, f005.1): the open is a mostly still switch stand under two stacked plates. Strip 2's 'gust of powder' doesn't show at phone size: across all 8 frames you mostly see a gentle camera push (8.2% changed). Nothing stops the scroll in the first 2 seconds, which costs Hook.

105.45s (filmstrip_the_freight_scale_needle_37): this is a hero 'boom' beat ('needle swings hard toward MOSTLY OPPOSED and bounces'), but the needle stays at upper-right in all 8 frames, with no swing, overshoot or settle. The only change is a MOSTLY OPPOSED plate popping in. The impact doesn't land in the object, which costs Motion.

108.8s (f108.8): the 'MOSTLY OPPOSED' label on the scale dial is crammed against the dial rim, with the M and D touching the bezel. The needle points upper-right, away from the label it is supposed to indicate. This costs Composition and Typography.

72.0-76.2s (filmstrip_5_bare_ties_then_30_laid_ties_on_the_27, f076.6): the VO says 'Count the ties. 30 days runs past December 7th', but during that line the DNR branch shows only faint bare-tie stubs, and the laid ties come in after it. Even then, only about 12 laid ties fit in frame before the edge, so a viewer can't count 30. The image payoff lags and undercuts the film's central device, which costs VO sync.

127.6-130s (filmstrip_the_second_switch_s_lever_holding_mi_45, 7.0% changed): the closing frames are close to a static hold. The 'lever holding mid-throw' and 'lamp flaring' are barely visible from frame to frame, so the question lands on a near-freeze rather than a performed beat. The RULES ties in the foreground sit flat and horizontal and don't follow the angle of the diverging rails, which reads as a perspective error on the last frame.

19.0s, 86.8s, 94.5s (f019.0, f086.8, f094.5): the faceless Suits have flat torso fills, ball hands and a stiff stance, and read plainer than the shaded switch stand, boxcars and binder stack in the same frames. This is a finish-parity gap that costs Illustration craft. They do get a walk-in (strip 5) and a pointing gesture (strip 29), but no visible breathing or weight shift while they stand still.
25.5s (f025.5): the 'NOV 27TH' table card is partly hidden behind the 'SET TO RESUME FRIDAY' plate, so a plate overlaps an in-art label and the card is cut off.
31.0s (f031.0): the 'NO DATA CENTER ITEM' sign on the buffer stop runs into the right edge of the frame, so the end of 'ITEM' is at the crop line. This is a crop risk, and worse in 4:5.

Throughout (f005.1, f019.0, f048.0, f056.1, f086.8, f094.5, f108.8, f117.4): the same foreground set dressing (snow mound, stacked ties, loose rail, steaming bucket, signal post) repeats in about 10 shots, and many frames carry 2 or 3 stacked plates plus the caption box. Shots look templated and top-heavy with text, which costs Composition and Illustration craft.

Post (out/dispatch/post.txt), 'Alaska can write its rules before a tenant arrives and court AI infrastructure money from firmer ground': this is an editorial position that leans one way. The film keeps it to the claim-supported 'stall no project AIDEA has named'. Ruaro's quote and the reversion clause give some balance, but the post's honest turn is thinner than the film's.
